items.title: Panama by Air (Reel 4)
items.creator: R. A. Duhem, Duhem and Harter Motion Picture Company
items.basis: Internet Archive public domain mark; released 1914
items.date_basis: flights of 25 and 27 April 1913, Canal Record VI no. 36, pp. 297-298 (F63); released 1914: read every intertitle for post-August wording before use
items.seen: Aerial views of the canal from a hydro-biplane, the Culebra Cut among them; the IA blurb's landing in Gatun Lake conflicts with the Record's Cristobal landing.
items.people: a hydro-biplane's aerial views; people only in the landing scenes at Colon (not used)
items.source_format: MPEG-2 PS as delivered (the largest file the source offers)
items.telecine_basis: ffmpeg idet on 20 s at 20 s (2026-11-08): repeated fields top 76, bottom 83 of 600 frames, multi-frame TFF 406, BFF 0: a 3:2 pulldown signature on a top-field-first NTSC transfer
items.intertitles: read on viewing: 'Panama Canal Part 4'; '2,500 ft. over Culebra Cut'; 'The towns of Culebra and Empire'; 'Camp Elliott on Gold Hill, the highest point in Culebra Cut'; 'The Panama Railway to the left'; Chagres, Matachin, Gatun Lake, dam, spillway, guide wall, the Atlantic channel, Limon Bay, 'We landed safe and sound in the Atlantic', 'Landing on Limon Bay at Colon'. None postdates the horizon; none is shown (the spans lie between them)
items.content_flags_basis: the whole reel viewed on contact sheets on 8 Nov 2026: no medical picture, no named patient (children appear in the 1906 street crowds, unnamed), no bodies or violence

items.title: President Taft's inspection of the Panama Canal (Signal Corps 111-M-331)
items.creator: United States Army Signal Corps
items.basis: a United States government work on the founder default of 8 Nov 2026; NARA 'Use Restriction: Undetermined' (read 8 Nov 2026). Viewed: the reel's own intertitles credit 'Feature Film M'f'g Co., Washington, D.C.', a private maker, so the Signal Corps premise needs the founder's ruling
items.date_basis: the catalogue's 1910 is impossible (the Arkansas was commissioned in September 1912); the Canal Record has Taft reach Cristobal on the Arkansas on 24 December 1912 and sail on the 26th (F64); viewed: Key West, the Arkansas, Culebra Cut, a slide, Miraflores and Pedro Miguel locks, Gatun Lake, the spillway, 'native life'; nothing seen postdates the horizon
items.seen: Taft addresses a crowd and embarks on the Arkansas at Key West; excavation, dredging, the Pedro Miguel and Miraflores locks, Gatun Lake, the spillway, 'native dwellings'.
items.people: the President's party at Key West and at the locks; crowds of visitors on the lock walls
items.source_format: MP4 as delivered (the largest file the source offers)
items.rights_checked: 2026-11-08: NARA catalog Use Restriction(s): Undetermined (Access: Unrestricted) (holds only on the founder default of 8 Nov 2026 (a Signal Corps production, a US government work); NARA itself says Undetermined)
items.extra_cuts_basis: the intertitle 'LAKE GATUN' from 483.43 to 491.30 s, which scdet (threshold 8) misses: placed on per-frame luma differences (2026-11-08)
items.intertitles: 'Reception at Mayor's House at Key West'; 'The President leaving Key West for the battleship Arkansas'; 'The President boarding the battleship "Arkansas" in Key West harbor'; 'Going into Culabra Cut'; 'Culebra Cut, showing steam-shovel handling a twelve-ton rock'; 'Ride through Culebra Cut on bottom of canal'; 'Slide in Culebra Cut'; 'Inspecting Milaflores lock, lock gates in operation'; 'Lake Gatun'; 'Pedro Miguel Locks'; 'Spillway of Gatun Dam in action'; 'Native life'; each signed Feature Film M'f'g Co., Washington, D.C.; the file ends on 'END OF RECORDING'
items.content_flags_basis: the whole reel viewed on contact sheets on 8 Nov 2026: no medical picture, no named patient (children appear in the 1906 street crowds, unnamed), no bodies or violence
